calib.cvep.briefing.1: All targets flicker with the same code, shifted for each one: this crackling is normal.
calib.cvep.briefing.2: Look at the target circled in blue, without moving your eyes, until the circle changes.
calib.cvep.briefing.3: Here, your gaze is what counts: keep it on the disc.
calib.cvep.briefing.4: Stay still and blink as little as possible.
calib.cvep.briefing.5: The circle regularly moves to another target. The first seconds after each change are ignored, while your gaze finds it.
calib.cvep.chiffres: {justesse} of targets recognized over {n_decisions} decisions ({n_cycles} cycles; chance: {hasard})
calib.cvep.comparaison.detail: p = {p:.3f} over {n} decision(s) where the two decoders differ ({b} eCCA only, {c} rCCA only)
calib.cvep.comparaison.gagnant: {gagnant} does better, and the gap is large enough not to come from chance ({detail})
calib.cvep.comparaison.impossible: the two decoders could not be compared: not enough consecutive cycles on the same target
calib.cvep.comparaison.indiscernables: the two decoders are INDISTINGUISHABLE ({detail}): their gap may come from chance, do not choose on this basis
calib.cvep.honnetete: With six targets, chance is 16.7%, not 50%. On this headset, with one person, we got 59.5% with eCCA and 64.9% with rCCA, by decoding offline the recordings of a training. Live, the engine adds two thresholds and a vote, so it often stays silent: on the same headset, it answered about 46% of the time, with 71% correct answers. So do not compare what you measure live with 59.5 / 64.9%. These references come from a single person: expect less.
calib.cvep.hors_bloc: {n} clock marker(s) arrived outside a block: was the stimulus window started by "Train"?
calib.cvep.label: Train the c-VEP
calib.cvep.non_mesure.conseil: Redo the training without interrupting it.
calib.cvep.non_mesure.raison: Not enough consecutive cycles on the same target to make a decision.
calib.cvep.param.bande.aide: The c-VEP response covers a wide frequency band, because the code can change at every frame. The low cutoff cannot go below {plancher:g} Hz: each training extract lasts only one cycle of the code (about 1 s). The thresholds of "Set up" ("Minimum correlation", "Margin over the second") are calibrated on 2-45 Hz. With another band, check them again with "Guided test". The model records the band and the mains-frequency notch, and decodes with the same filter.
calib.cvep.trop_pauvre: Session too small to train: {n} extract(s) over {cibles} target(s); at least {min_epoques} over {min_cibles} targets are needed. {hors_bloc}Redo the session and check the contact: lost extracts give this result.
calib.cvep.verdict.faible: WEAK — try again: add salt water to Pz/PO7/Oz/PO8, and keep your gaze on the circled disc, without wandering.
calib.cvep.verdict.non_mesure: Accuracy not measured: a decision needs {cycles} consecutive cycles on the same target, and the session does not contain them. The models exist, but we do not know what they are worth: train again without interrupting the session.
calib.cvep.verdict.repere: GOOD, like the best session obtained on this headset (59.5 / 64.9%)
calib.errp.briefing.1: A dot must reach the green pad: that is its goal.
calib.errp.briefing.2: At each step, it moves one square, most often toward the pad.
calib.errp.briefing.3: Sometimes it goes the wrong way, on purpose: that is an error, and it is what we record.
calib.errp.briefing.4: Follow the dot with your eyes and wish it arrives: you have nothing else to do.
calib.errp.briefing.5: Do not anticipate the errors: the brain reacts to a surprise, and watching for the next one erases it.
calib.errp.briefing.6: Stay still and blink as little as possible when the dot moves.
calib.errp.chiffres: Error / correct-command separation: {auc} (chance: 0.50) · {tnr} of correct commands kept, {tpr} of errors caught ({n} trials, including {n_erreurs} errors)
calib.errp.honnetete: With the default setting, this detector catches one error in two and wrongly cancels one correct command in seven (on this headset, with one person). That is what an error potential read on a single trial with dry electrodes is worth, not a bad setting. These two rates are optimistic: the threshold was chosen on the same scores that measure them. In real use, expect to cancel more correct commands. The "AUC" value (the ability to separate errors from correct commands) is honest: 0.776 for this person (0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect; 200 trials). Do not conclude anything from one trial or from ten: out of ten errors, catching five is the expected result; eight or two stay within the noise.
calib.errp.label: Train the ErrP
calib.errp.non_mesure.raison: Not enough trials of each type to measure the score on trials the model has not seen.
calib.errp.param.bande.aide: The filter applied to the second after each step of the dot. The ErrP is a slow wave, especially between 1 and 8 Hz. Raising the low cutoff removes drift, but also part of the wave. Raising the high cutoff mostly adds noise. The model records this filter and will always decode with it: to change it, train again. When in doubt, keep the default value.
calib.errp.reserve.non_significatif: Indistinguishable from chance with this number of trials: redo a longer session. This is not a contact problem.
calib.errp.trop_pauvre: Session too small to train: {n} epoch(s), {corrects} correct and {erreurs} error(s). At least {min_total} in total are needed, including {min_classe} of each type: otherwise the mode cannot set its threshold. Redo a longer session and check the contact: lost trials give this result.
calib.errp.verdict.bon: GOOD for an ErrP read on a single trial — on par with what one person reached on this headset (0.776)
calib.errp.verdict.faible: WEAK — try again: add salt water to Fz, Cz and Pz, and above all do not anticipate the errors (the brain reacts to a surprise).
calib.errp.verdict.non_mesure: Separation not measured: not enough trials of each type to compute it on trials the model has not seen.
calib.errp.verdict.non_significatif: {mot} — this score may come from chance with this number of trials (p = {p:.3f}). Redo a longer session before relying on it; this is not a contact problem.
calib.fenetre.absente: The stimulus window did not announce itself within {attente:.0f} s: it did not start, or it publishes on a stream other than "{flux}".
calib.fenetre.chauffe: The headset is settling: the stimulus window is about to take over.
calib.fenetre.essais: The session runs in the stimulus window: follow its cues.
calib.fenetre.muette: The stimulus window has not responded for {silence:.0f} s, in the middle of the session: {essai} epoch(s) recorded out of {annonces} announced. Nothing is trained or saved.
calib.mi.briefing.1: At the start of each trial, a beep sounds and the screen shows the task to imagine. For LEFT, RIGHT and REST, the beep also indicates the task: left ear = left fist, right ear = right fist, both ears (longer beep) = rest.
calib.mi.briefing.2: Start imagining at the beep, and keep going until the countdown ends.
calib.mi.briefing.3: Feel the movement from the inside (the tension of the muscle, for example in the forearm for a fist), without moving.
calib.mi.briefing.4: Keep this sensation for the whole trial, continuously or by repeating it, not just once at the start.
calib.mi.briefing.5: Tip: really make each movement 3 or 4 times before starting, to memorize the sensation.
calib.mi.briefing.6: Stay still, keep your eyes on the "+" cross and blink as little as possible while you imagine.
calib.mi.briefing.7: Rest: do nothing special, relax and breathe normally.
calib.mi.chiffres.sans_seuil: — with {n} trials, a real result cannot be told apart from chance
calib.mi.chiffres.seuil: — at least {seuil} is needed to do better than chance
calib.mi.honnetete: This score is measured on trials the model did not see during its learning: it predicts what it will do in real use. For comparison: on this headset, with one person, we got 63% with two tasks (left and right fists) and 40% with three (adding rest). For other tasks, there is no reference yet. Motor imagery does not work equally well for everyone: a modest score is normal, and it is not a mistake on your part.
calib.mi.label: Train Motor Imagery
calib.mi.non_mesure.conseil: Redo the session with more trials per task.
calib.mi.non_mesure.raison: Not enough trials per task to measure the score on trials the model has not seen.
calib.mi.param.bande.aide: Motor Imagery reads the rhythms of the motor cortex: mu (8-12 Hz) and beta (13-30 Hz). Stay between 4 Hz (below: drift and eye movements) and 40 Hz (above: muscle tension). The model keeps this filter, and will decode with the same one.
calib.mi.param.fbcsp.aide: A variant that splits the band into slices of about 4 Hz and keeps those that best distinguish your tasks. Then widen the band (for example 4-40 Hz) to leave it room to choose. Never measured as useful on this headset. A short test is not enough to tell whether it does better: compare two trainings done in the same session.
calib.mi.param.fbcsp.label: FBCSP (filter bank)
calib.mi.param.mise_en_route.aide: The time between the beep and the start of the recording: the time to properly start imagining the movement. 3 s by default (it often takes about 2 s to get going well). The model keeps this value, and "Guided test" reuses it. To find your own, train and test a model at 3 s then at 1 s, in the same session.
calib.mi.param.mise_en_route.label: Lead-in
calib.mi.param.shrinkage.aide: A more robust version of the last stage of the model, useful when there are few trials for a lot of information to combine (FBCSP, 4 or 5 tasks, short session). On this headset, no difference has been measured. To know whether it helps you, compare two trainings done in the same session.
calib.mi.param.shrinkage.label: Regularized LDA (shrinkage)
calib.mi.param.taches.aide: One task per field, from 2 to 5 (for example FEET and HANDS). During the trial, the screen shows the task to imagine. The model learns these tasks, and your application receives them under these names (decoded_mi stream): choose short names, without commas. LEFT, RIGHT and REST keep their detailed instruction and their left or right beep; the other tasks have a beep in the center. Without REST, the model always chooses one of the tasks: add REST if your application must know when you do nothing.
calib.mi.param.taches.label: Tasks to imagine
calib.mi.param.trials_per_class.aide: The number of trials for each task. Longer is not always better: fatigue lowers results late in the session. Start with the default value.
calib.mi.param.trials_per_class.label: Trials per task
calib.mi.reserve.non_significatif: With so few trials, this score may come from chance: do not keep this model, redo the session.
calib.mi.trop_court: Not enough data to train: {comptes} trials per task; at least {minimum} are needed (some trials may have been lost during the session). Redo a longer session.
calib.mi.verdict.faible: WEAK — try again: check the electrode contact, stay still, and feel the movement instead of imagining it as a picture.
calib.mi.verdict.non_mesurable: Score impossible to measure: not enough trials per task.
calib.mi.verdict.non_significatif: {mot} — with {n} trials, this score may come from chance ({p}). Do not keep this model: redo the session, rested.
calib.p300.briefing.1: Look at the target circled in blue for the whole round: it is by looking at it that your brain produces the P300 wave.
calib.p300.briefing.2: The six targets light up one at a time, in brief flashes, in random order.
calib.p300.briefing.3: Counting the flashes of your target helps you stay attentive, but it is not required.
calib.p300.briefing.4: Stay still and blink as little as possible during the flashes. You can blink between rounds.
calib.p300.briefing.5: The target changes at each round: the stimulus window tells you which one.
calib.p300.honnetete: The figure that decides is the selection: does the model find the target of a round it did not see during its training? One or two errors out of six are normal, because P300 is read by averaging the repeated flashes. A second figure, the AUC, judges a single flash (target/non-target). On this headset, with one person, we got 0.71 over 576 epochs: that is what a P300 is worth with dry electrodes, not a failure. Both figures are measured round by round: no epoch is used both to learn and to test.
calib.p300.label: Train the P300
calib.p300.non_mesure.raison: Not enough rounds to set one aside.
calib.p300.param.bande.aide: The filter applied to each epoch (about 1 s around each flash). The P300 is a slow wave, especially between 1 and 8 Hz. Raising the low cutoff removes drift, but also part of the wave. Raising the high cutoff mostly adds noise. The model records this filter and always decodes with it: to change it, train again. When in doubt, keep the default.
calib.p300.trop_pauvre: Session too small to train: {n} epoch(s) over {manches} round(s), {classes} class(es). At least {min_epoques} over {min_manches} rounds are needed, with targets and non-targets. Redo a longer session and check the contact: lost epochs give this result.
calib.p300.verdict.faible: WEAK — try again: add salt water to the electrodes and keep your eyes on the circled target (counting its flashes helps).
calib.p300.verdict.non_mesure: Selection not measured: not enough rounds to set one aside.
mode.cvep.desaccord.cibles: This model was trained with {modele} targets, but the stimulus shows {actuel}: it no longer matches. Train it again ("Train" on the c-VEP page).
mode.cvep.desaccord.code: This model expects a code of {modele} frames, but the stimulus shows one of {actuel} (code on {bits} bits): it no longer matches. Train it again ("Train" on the c-VEP page).
mode.cvep.label: c-VEP
mode.cvep.modele.autres_codes: This model was trained with codes other than the ones shown today ({quoi}): it no longer matches. Train it again ("Train" on the c-VEP page). File: {nom}
mode.cvep.modele.codes_contenu: the codes or their order changed since training; shift between targets: {rotation}
mode.cvep.modele.codes_dimensions: it has {forme} codes, the stimulus shows {attendu}
mode.cvep.modele.decodeur_inconnu: This file declares an unknown decoder ({decodeur}, expected: {attendus}): it comes from a newer version, or it was edited by hand. File: {nom}
mode.cvep.modele.incomplet: This file is not a c-VEP {decodeur} model (missing: {manquantes}). File: {nom}
mode.cvep.motif.reference_perimee: clock too old: the stimulus window is no longer publishing (closed? crashed?)
mode.cvep.motif.sans_reference: no clock signal received: open the c-VEP stimulus window and check that it publishes on the "Marker stream" you set
mode.cvep.motif.sous_les_seuils: correlations too weak or too close between targets: check the contact, add salt water to the electrodes, and look at a single target
mode.cvep.motif.vote_non_conclu: the last windows do not point to the same target: look at a single target without moving your eyes
mode.cvep.param.corr_min.aide: The correlation the best target must exceed to be kept (the higher it is, the more the signal looks like that target's code). The default is strict: a threshold that is too low makes the mode decode noise with confidence. If the mode stays silent despite good contact, lower it. The change takes effect at once, without restarting the mode.
mode.cvep.param.corr_min.label: Minimum correlation
mode.cvep.param.margin.aide: The lead the best target must have over the second. Together with "Minimum correlation", it forms a single rule: if you loosen one without the other, the other one decides alone. It can also be adjusted during a session.
mode.cvep.param.margin.label: Margin over second
mode.cvep.param.min_votes.aide: How many of these windows must point to the same target for the mode to publish it. The more there are, the slower but the more reliable. Do not go above "Vote windows": the mode would never decide anything.
mode.cvep.param.model.aide: The model made by your training, newest first. Each training produces two, to choose from: the eCCA compares your signal to the average recorded response for each target; the rCCA learns your response to a single change of frame, then deduces the expected response for each target. The model is specific to one person: someone else's gives plausible but wrong correlations. Empty list? Click "Train" on this page.
mode.cvep.param.stream_in.aide: The stream where the c-VEP stimulus window publishes its clock (about once a second). Without it, nothing is decoded. Not in the list? Leave the page and come back. Applies only at the next start of the mode.
mode.cvep.param.vote_len.aide: The number of recent windows that vote before the mode publishes a target. At 5 windows per second, 3 windows add 0.6 s of delay. At 1, there is no vote: more responsive, but much noisier.
mode.cvep.pyntbci_manquant: The c-VEP rCCA decoder needs the Python package pyntbci, which is not installed: install it with "pip install -r requirements.txt". The eCCA models can still be used.
mode.cvep.summary: One target out of several, each flashing with its own shifted code (the fastest mode).
mode.errp.cause.cv_echouee: the calculation on unseen trials failed for all the settings tried ({reglages}), on {n} trials. This is not a lack of trials: one flat or loose electrode is enough to make it fail. Check the contact, then train again.
mode.errp.cause.trop_courte: training too short: {n} trials ({corrects} correct, {erreurs} errors). At least 10 are needed, with at least 2 of each
mode.errp.label: ErrP
mode.errp.modele.cause_inconnue: cause not recorded: model created before training recorded it
mode.errp.modele.noyau_herite: The core of this model, which computes its scores, comes from an old version (module {module}, expected {attendu}). Train it again: in the console, click "Train" on the ErrP page. File: {nom}
mode.errp.modele.sans_oof: This model has no out-of-fold scores, that is, scores computed on trials it has not seen ({cause}): no threshold can be set. Train it again: in the console, click "Train" on the ErrP page. File: {nom}
mode.errp.param.model.aide: The model made by your training. It is specific to one person: someone else's gives plausible but wrong verdicts. Empty list? Click "Train" on this page.
mode.errp.param.stream_in.aide: The stream where your application publishes the moment of each feedback shown. Not in the list? Leave the page and come back. Applies only at the next start of the mode.
mode.errp.param.tnr_target.aide: The share of correct commands to keep. The engine derives its threshold from your training. The higher it is, the fewer correct commands it cancels, but the fewer errors it catches. Reference: keeping 95 % of correct commands catches only 24 % of errors; 85 % catches 50 %, 70 % catches 71 %.
mode.errp.param.tnr_target.label: Correct commands kept
mode.errp.sans_scores_oof: This model has no out-of-fold scores, that is, scores computed on trials it has not seen ({cause}): no threshold can be set on it. Train it again: in the console, click "Train" on the ErrP page.
mode.errp.summary: After each feedback shown, tells whether the machine has just made a mistake, based on the brain's error wave.
mode.geometrie.desaccord: This model was trained with a different signal segmentation than the engine's ({ecarts}): its scores would look plausible but be wrong. Train it again: in the console, click "Train" on the {mode} page.
mode.mi.label: Motor Imagery
mode.mi.param.min_votes.aide: How many recent windows must point to the same task for the mode to announce it. More = slower, but more reliable. Never more than "Vote windows": the mode would never answer.
mode.mi.param.model.aide: The model made by your training. It only works for you: someone else's gives answers that look plausible but are wrong. Empty list? Click "Train" on this page.
mode.mi.param.prob_min.aide: The minimum confidence for a window to count in the vote. Higher = more cautious: the mode answers less often, but makes fewer mistakes.
mode.mi.param.prob_min.label: Minimum probability
mode.mi.param.vote_len.aide: How many recent windows vote (5 windows per second: 5 windows = 1 s). The Motor Imagery signal is noisy: a slightly longer vote steadies it.
mode.mi.summary: Recognize the movement you imagine (left hand, right hand… your choice), without moving.
mode.modele.aucun: You have not chosen a model: in the console, click "Train" on the {mode} page.
mode.modele.herite: Model from an old version (module {module}, expected {attendu}), refused on purpose. Train it again: in the console, click "Train" on the {mode} page. File: {nom}
mode.modele.pas_un_modele: This file is not a {mode} model: {nom}
mode.neuro.label: Neuro
mode.neuro.param.rebaseline_s.aide: Slowly resets the zero to follow the drift of dry electrodes. The value is the length of the reset, in seconds. 0 = zero fixed. If too short, the reset would also erase the mental states you want to observe.
mode.neuro.param.rebaseline_s.label: Rest baseline reset
mode.neuro.param.smoothing.aide: Smooths the three indices over time. 0 = raw and jittery; 0.95 = very smooth but slow to react. The indices are noisy: the default smooths a lot.
mode.neuro.param.smoothing.label: Smoothing
mode.neuro.summary: Mental load, drowsiness and engagement, as a deviation from today's rest.
mode.p300.label: P300
mode.p300.modele.herite: Model from an old version (module {module}, expected {attendu}), refused on purpose: it must be retrained from the kept calibration epochs. File: {nom}
mode.p300.param.model.aide: The model made by your training. It is specific to one person: someone else's gives scores that look plausible but are wrong. Empty list? Click "Train" on this page.
mode.p300.param.stream_in.aide: The stream where your application publishes the moment of each flash. Not in the list? Leave the page and come back. This setting only applies at the next start of the mode.
mode.p300.summary: Choose one target out of 6 that light up one at a time (P300 wave).
mode.param.min_votes.label: Agreeing votes
mode.param.modele.label: Trained model
mode.param.stream_in.label: Marker stream
mode.param.vote_len.label: Vote windows
mode.raw.label: Raw
mode.raw.summary: The 8 EEG channels as the headset returns them, in µV at 250 Hz.
mode.ssvep.label: SSVEP
mode.ssvep.param.alpha_hz.aide: The alpha peak varies from person to person (6 to 14 Hz, 9.6 Hz on average): a target placed on it blends in with rest, and the suggested frequencies move away from it. To measure yours, click "Measure" (~40 s), then "Apply". Changing it does not redo the rest.
mode.ssvep.param.alpha_hz.label: Person's alpha peak
mode.ssvep.param.bande.aide: The filter applied to the signal before decoding ({bas}-{haut} Hz by default). It must let through your frequencies and their harmonics (2 and 3 times the frequency): narrowing the band removes noise, but also signal. Limits: not below {plancher} Hz (the filter would not have time to settle within the window), not above {plafond} Hz (a target would fall into the mains filter, 50 or 60 Hz). Changing it redoes the rest, and both tests use it.
mode.ssvep.param.cibles.aide: What your targets flash on. On a screen, each frequency must be a whole-number divisor of its refresh rate. With physical targets (LEDs driven by a board such as an Arduino), any frequency in the band is possible: the refresh rate no longer matters, and "Suggest" picks frequencies in half-hertz steps. Both "Test" buttons show their targets on screen: they only work with a screen.
mode.ssvep.param.cibles.label: Targets shown on
mode.ssvep.param.freqs.aide: The frequencies your application flashes, one per target. Each must divide the screen's refresh rate (at 60 Hz: 30, 20, 15, 12, 10, 8.571…) and stay far from your alpha peak. Changing this list recreates the stream: your clients must subscribe again.
mode.ssvep.param.freqs.label: Target frequencies
mode.ssvep.param.refresh_hz.aide: The refresh rate of the screen that shows the targets, not necessarily this one: your application may run elsewhere. The possible frequencies are its whole-number divisors. After changing it, click "Suggest", under the alpha peak: it computes a set of frequencies for this screen, without redoing the rest. With physical targets, it no longer matters.
mode.ssvep.param.refresh_hz.label: Stimulus screen refresh rate
mode.ssvep.param.z_min.aide: How far a target's signal must rise above the resting noise level (in standard deviations) to be announced. Lower: more announcements, but more errors. Higher: fewer announcements, but safer. Default 2.5. It is set in the "1. Set up" block of the mode; both tests use it, and that is where you see its effect.
mode.ssvep.param.z_min.label: Detection threshold
mode.ssvep.summary: Which flashing target the user is looking at, about 5 times per second.
mode.ssvep.tests_ecran: Both tests show their targets on screen: they do not work with physical targets. To check your LEDs, start the mode and look at what your application receives ("What your app sees", on the home page).
